title: Letterpress word game
lede: Loren Brichter’s 2012 iPhone game of colored letter tiles, drawn after Windows Phone and cited as an inspiration for iOS 7.
summary: A 5 × 5 board of flat letter tiles that turn blue or red as players claim them. Atebits, 2012.

evidence.note: Wikipedia article read on 2026-09-28. A Wayback copy of atebits.com/letterpress (30 November 2012) shows a small promotional image of the board; it is too small to count as observed and was not kept.

styles.note: A link between Metro and iOS 7: its interface borrows from Windows Phone, and Apple’s designers cited it for iOS 7.

context: Letterpress is a turn-based word game developed by Loren Brichter and published by Atebits, released for iOS on 24 October 2012. Players claim letter tiles on a 5 × 5 grid; claimed tiles take the player’s color ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letterpress_(video_game))).
“For graphics and the user interface, he took inspiration from the Windows Phone.”
It won a 2013 Apple Design Award, and “Apple designer Jony Ive took inspiration from minimalist iOS apps, among them Letterpress, while designing graphics for iOS 7.”
The Verge described the interface as “barren” with “natural-feeling animations”.
interpretation: It shows the flat grammar moving from Microsoft to Apple’s platform through a third-party app, before [iOS 7](ref:ios-7-interface-2013).
